title: Sparse Embedding for Interpretable Hospital Admission Prediction
rationale: Gate 1/2 pass (ED/hospital-admission EHR prediction at individual-patient level); Gate 3 fails -- no clinician interacts with or evaluates the system/explanations, purely downstream statistical evaluation. F2 passes: k-sparse autoencoder + t-SNE explicitly framed as post-hoc interpretability/feature-attribution contribution. F3 also fails: predictive performance (AUROC/RMSE) is evaluated but the XAI component itself (t-SNE plots, feature-importance charts) is only qualitative/narrated demonstration -- no proxy metrics (fidelity/stability), no human evaluation. MethodPaper exception does not apply -- no deliberate/systematic evaluation of the interpretability component, treated as incidental decoration. F4/F5 pass (full IEEE proceedings, sufficient methodological detail). Both Gate 3 (E1) and F3 (E3) fail; E1 assigned per the protocol's explicit priority tie-break (lowest-numbered code wins when multiple exclusion reasons apply), overriding the original E3 call.

title: Early Risk Prediction for Emergency Department Triage using Machine Learning Techniques
rationale: All three gates pass: ED triage domain, individual-patient severity classification, and a genuine clinician-in-loop deployment (triage-assistant UI feeding predicted severity/queue order/explanations directly to clinical staff). F2 passes: dedicated SHAP explainability layer over LightGBM/XGBoost/Random Forest predictions. F3 fails: downstream classification metrics (accuracy/precision/recall/F1) and queue-latency are evaluated, but the SHAP outputs themselves (summary plot, force plot) are only qualitative case-study illustrations -- no fidelity/faithfulness/stability proxy metrics, no clinician trust or comprehension study. MethodPaper exception does not apply -- applied system using an existing XAI framework (SHAP) without evaluating the explanation itself, not a novel XAI method with its own evaluation. No gate conflict this time (all three pass), so E3 applies cleanly with no priority tie-break needed.

title: A new machine learning technique for predicting traumatic injuries outcomes based on the vital signs
rationale: Gate 1/2 pass (ED/pre-hospital trauma domain, individual-patient 30-day mortality prediction from vital signs). Gate 3 fails: MAKER-RIMER hybrid model developed/evaluated purely offline on the TARN database, no clinical workflow integration or clinician interaction, simulated or real. F2 passes: hybrid Evidential Reasoning + Belief Rule-Based (RIMER) architecture explicitly framed as a transparent/interpretable design contribution. F3 also fails: predictive performance evaluated via 30-fold CV/AUC against LR/ANN/SVM/RF baselines, but the belief-rule tables themselves are only shown as static lookup configurations -- no fidelity/consistency/sparsity proxy metrics, no human evaluation with trauma clinicians. MethodPaper exception does not apply -- no deliberate evaluation of the interpretability mechanism beyond displaying the rule tables. F4/F5 pass. Both Gate 3 (E1) and F3 (E3) fail; E1 correctly assigned per the priority tie-break (lowest-numbered code wins), consistent with the 601300087 correction.
